NOTE:  PUBLIC PARTICIPATION INFORMATION
  Agenda reports and other disclosable public records relating to each Open Session agenda item are
  available on the City's website under City Council Meeting agendas at rhe.city and during regular
  business hours in the office of the City Clerk. Meetings are live broadcast on the City's website and a
  recording is available for viewing after each meeting. Meetings are also broadcast on PVP-TV Channel 35
  (Cox) and Channel 39 (Verizon).

  Public Comment is welcome in-person on any item during City Council consideration of the item. Public
  correspondence may also be emailed to the City Clerk at laurenp@rollinghillsestates.gov. Emails
  received before 3:00 p.m. prior to the start of the meeting will be forwarded to the City Council for their
  consideration and included as part of the record. Members of the public may also comment online using
  eComment on the “Meeting Agendas, Minutes & Videos” page of the City’s website
  (www.rhe.city/MeetingAgendas). Once the agenda is published, there will be an “eComment” button next
  to the linked agenda under "Upcoming Events". Follow this link to the City’s SpeakUp page. After you
  register, you may comment on any item on that particular agenda. These comments can be seen by the
  public, will be considered by the Council and become part of the record.

  An opportunity is also provided for the public to comment on non-agenda items concerning City matters. If
  you would like to address the City Council regarding an item on this agenda or make a general public
  comment, please complete a speaker sheet and give to the City Clerk.

3.  ROLL CALL

City Council Members Absent:  Schmitz, Zerunyan

  City Attorney Don Davis
  Assistant City Manager Alexa Davis

8.  NEW BUSINESS

A.  AWARD OF PUBLIC WORKS CONTRACT TO E.C. CONSTRUCTION COMPANY TO
  INSTALL  STORMWATER  DETENTION  BASIN  AND  DIVERSION
  INFRASTRUCTURE ON PALOS VERDES DRIVE NORTH (SOUTH SIDE OF
  STREET, WEST OF ROLLING HILLS ROAD)

  Recommendation: That the City Council direct staff to enter into a Public Works
  Contract with E.C. Construction (all to the satisfaction of the City Attorney), to
  undertake the PVDN Storm Water Detention Basin Project, under the project
  supervision of Willdan Engineering, in the amount of $76,705, plus a $20,000
  contingency, for a grand total of $96,705.

Public Works Director Wahba provided a staff report (as per the agenda material.)

Public Works Director Wahba explained that there would be little to no traffic impacts from this
project in response to COUNCIL MEMBER SCHACHTER. He further explained that the project
is estimated to take approximately 30 days.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  2
MARCH 28, 2023
 Public Works Director Wahba explained that the project will be finished with a natural
vegetative slope, and that there is not currently a bridle trail or walking path is this area, in
response to COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA.

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chambers, via email and via eComment.
No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHACHTER moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  STEGURA, TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  DIRECT STAFF TO ENTER INTO A PUBLIC WORKS CONTRACT WITH E.C.
  CONSTRUCTION (ALL TO THE SATISFACTION OF THE CITY ATTORNEY),
  TO UNDERTAKE THE PVDN STORM WATER DETENTION BASIN
  PROJECT, UNDER THE PROJECT SUPERVISION OF WILLDAN
  ENGINEERING, IN THE AMOUNT OF $76,705, PLUS A $20,000
  CONTINGENCY, FOR A GRAND TOTAL OF $96,705.

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Stegura
  ABSENT:  Schmitz, Zerunyan

B.  RESOLUTION NO. 2542 - AUTHORIZING THE CITY OF ROLLING HILLS ESTATES
  TO TRANSFER $18,970 OF ITS RULE 20A ALLOCATION TO THE CITY OF
  ROLLING HILLS

  Recommendation: That the City Council approve Resolution No. 2542, authorizing
  the City of Rolling Hills Estates to gift $18,970 of its Rule 20A allocation to the City
  of Rolling Hills and authorize the City Manager to provide SCE with an official letter
  of transfer to the City of Rolling Hills citing the mutual benefit to both communities

Management Analyst Slawson provided a staff report (as per the agenda material.)

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chambers, via email and via eComment.
No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  SCHACHTER, TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL
  VOTE:

  APPROVE RESOLUTION NO. 2542, AUTHORIZING THE CITY OF ROLLING
  HILLS ESTATES TO GIFT $18,970 OF ITS RULE 20A ALLOCATION TO THE
  CITY OF ROLLING HILLS AND AUTHORIZE THE CITY MANAGER TO
  PROVIDE SCE WITH AN OFFICIAL LETTER OF TRANSFER TO THE CITY
  OF ROLLING HILLS CITING THE MUTUAL BENEFIT TO BOTH
  COMMUNITIES.

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Stegura
  ABSENT:  Schmitz, Zerunyan

City Clerk Pettit read Resolution No. 2542 by title.

C.  TRAFFIC & SAFETY COMMITTEE MEETING OF 2/21/2023 ACTION ITEMS

  Recommendation: That the City Council approve 1) the horse crossing signs
  proposed for Masongate Drive, and 2) the traffic calming related signs on Palos
  Verdes Drive East, for a total cost not to exceed $25,000. Staff further recommends
  that no action be taken at this time by the City Council for the installation of “No Right
  Turn” signs on Palos Verdes Drive North & East.

Public Works Director Wahba provided a staff report (as per the agenda material.)

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  3
MARCH 28, 2023
 Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chambers, via email and via eComment.
Public testimony was received from John Owens and Lynn Yen.

COUNCIL MEMBER SCHACHTER emphasized how limited the visibility is for both
pedestrians and those on horses.

Traffic Engineer Joanne Itagaki of Willdan Engineering explained the pedestrian count analysis
for the crosswalk, and also highlighted the option for a “turning vehicles yield to pedestrians”
sign. She then discussed a variety of options discussed at the Traffic & Safety Committee
meeting.

COUNCIL MEMBER SCHACHTER suggested doing a count of the cars that back up for the
right turn in the morning hours.

COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA suggested adding a “yield to pedestrians” sign in the interim
while taking the item back to the Traffic & Safety Committee for further consideration. Engineer
Itagaki also suggest adding flags to the new sign for additional visibility.

  COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  SCHACHTER, TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL
  VOTE:

  DIRECT STAFF TO BRING THE “NO RIGHT TURN” SIGNS ON PALOS
  VERDES DRIVE NORTH & EAST ITEM BACK TO THE TRAFFIC & SAFETY
  COMMITTEE FOR FURTHER CONSIDERATION, WHILE ADDING A “YIELD
  TO PEDESTRIANS” SIGN ADORNED WITH FLAGS AT THE
  RECOMMENDATION OF THE CITY’S TRAFFIC ENGINEER IN THE INTERIM.

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Stegura
  ABSENT:  Schmitz, Zerunyan

COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA suggested horse crossing pavement markings in addition to
the proposed signs for Masongate Drive.

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHACHTER moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  STEGURA, TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  APPROVE 1) THE HORSE CROSSING SIGNS PROPOSED FOR
  MASONGATE DRIVE AND DIRECTED STAFF TO BRING ITEM BACK TO
  THE TRAFFIC & SAFETY COMMITTEE FOR CONSIDERATION OF HORSE
  CROSSING PAVEMENT MARKINGS; AND APPROVE 2) THE TRAFFIC
  CALMING RELATED SIGNS ON PALOS VERDES DRIVE EAST, FOR A
  TOTAL COST NOT TO EXCEED $25,000.

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Stegura
  ABSENT:  Schmitz, Zerunyan

9.  OLD BUSINESS

None.

10.  CITY ATTORNEY ITEMS

None.

11.  CITY COUNCIL/REGIONAL COMMITTEE REPORTS

COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA attended the South Bay Cities Council of Governments
(SBCCOG) General Assembly last week along with MAYOR HUFF, staff and several
Commissioners.

MAYOR HUFF attended the Neighborhood Watch meeting last week, the California
Association of Councils of Governments (CALCOG) Regional Leadership Forum earlier in the

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  4
MARCH 28, 2023
 month, threw out the first pitch for Silver Spur Little League’s Opening Day, attended the ribbon
cutting for the School of Rock, and attended the Children and Family Garden Groundbreaking
and Reception at South Coast Botanic Garden.

12.  MAYOR AND COUNCIL ITEMS

A.  AUTHORIZATION TO ATTEND THE CALIFORNIA CONTRACT  CITIES
  ASSOCIATION'S ANNUAL MUNICIPAL SEMINAR MAY 18-21

  CONSENSUS OF COUNCIL TO ALLOW ANY/ALL COUNCIL MEMBERS TO
  ATTEND.

B.  SUPPORT LETTER FOR ASSEMBLY BILL 1538 (AB 1538)

  Recommendation: That the City Council authorize the Mayor to sign a letter on behalf
  of the City of Rolling Hills Estates in support of AB 1538, establishing a Clean Energy
  Reliability Program.

Community Development Director Naughton provided a staff report (as per the agenda
material.)

  COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  SCHACHTER, TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL
  VOTE:

  AUTHORIZE THE MAYOR TO SIGN A LETTER ON BEHALF OF THE CITY
  OF ROLLING HILLS ESTATES IN SUPPORT OF AB 1538, ESTABLISHING A
  CLEAN ENERGY RELIABILITY PROGRAM.

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Stegura
  ABSENT:  Schmitz, Zerunyan

13.  CLOSED SESSION

None.

14.  ADJOURNMENT

At 8:13 PM MAYOR HUFF adjourned the City Council meeting in memory of the children
and teachers killed in the mass shooting in Nashville, Tennessee this week. The meeting
was adjourned to Tuesday, April 25, 2023, at 7:00 p.m. for the purpose of a Regular Meeting.

Submitted by,  Approved by,

Lauren Pettit  Britt Huff
